newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner seals $1 bln offshore Norway deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner seals $1 bln offshore Norway deal.

text.p: Norwegian engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA said on Friday it had won a $1 billion contract to build the largest ever floating gas production platform for Norway's offshore Aasgard development.
Awarded by state Norwegian oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, the turnkey contract is the biggest to be placed in the Norwegian offshore sector.
Kvaerner's A share price rose briefly in light trade to an intraday high at 309 crowns, a rise of four crown. The Bs also advanced four crowns to hit a peak at 278 crowns.
Kvaerner will be responsible for project management, engineering, construction and installation of the Aasgard B gas platform, the first such structure on the Norwegian shelf.
The London-based company said construction would begin in March 1998 at Kvaerner Rosenborg's yard in Stavanger on the west coast of Norway.
The platform is due to be delivered at the field, which lies off mid-Norway in the Norwegian Sea, on August 16, 2000 and will begin production on October 1.

Measuring 96 metres by 115 metres, the topside will weigh 28,000 tonnes with living quarters and processing facilities. The hull will weigh 17,000 tonnes and will be held in position in a water depth of 300 metres by 16 mooring lines and anchors.
Each mooring line will be 1,400 metres long and will weigh 400 tonnes.

Aasgard will have a daily export capacity of 38 million cubic metres of gas and 94,000 barrels of condensate. In addition it will pump 41,000 barrels per day of partially stabilised oil, which will be transported to the Aasgard A production ship, and 11 million cubic metres of gas per day for reinjection into the reservoir.

Licensees in the Aasgard development are operator Statoil with 60.5 percent, Norsk Agip 7.85 percent, Total Norge 7.65 percent, Mobil Development Norway 7.35 percent, Neste Petroleum and Saga Petroleum with 7.00 percent and Norsk Hydro 2.6 percent.
